subject: project:gdl
value: TWO MEASUREMENT FAILURES, ONE ROOT CAUSE: THE PROBE LOOP ARBITRATES A STATE AGAINST THE PREVIOUS STATE, SO A BAD KEEP BECOMES THE YARDSTICK FOR EVERY LATER PROBE. FIRST CLAUSE: probe.py's IMPROVED verdict is not sufficient evidence to bank. The mandate requires fresh fuzzy on a CONFLICT, and CONFLICT is defined as real and the opcode multiset DISAGREEING -- so the one shape the mandate does not cover is real and multiset AGREEING while fuzzy falls. Measured on do_players: an edit naming a byte offset as an s32 local moved real 1092 -> 1091 AND the multiset 20t -> 19t AND the instruction count 1170 -> 1171 toward the target's 1174, so probe.py printed `IMPROVED [best updated]` and banked it as the revert point. Its fresh fuzzy was 94.4804 against the previous state's 94.9387 -- a 0.4583 REGRESSION that all three primary arbiters called an improvement, because the edit replaced a displacement pair with a pointer add that read further from target while shortening the linear diff. SECOND CLAUSE, AND THE MORE EXPENSIVE ONE: once that state was banked, the NEXT probe was measured on top of it and its verdict inverted. The same predicate-extraction edit measured 94.9106 stacked on the bad keep -- a loss against 94.9387, and it would have been recorded as a refuted axis -- and 95.2683 when the tree was first restored to the last COMMITTED state and the identical edit applied alone. The edit was worth +0.3296 fuzzy and five multiset tokens; stacked, it read as -0.0281. A banked state that no gate ever rejected silently converted a win into a park. THE RULE: measure fresh fuzzy before banking ANY state whose keep decision rests on real or the multiset, not only on a CONFLICT; and when a probe lands on a base that was itself banked without a fuzzy measurement, re-run it from the last COMMITTED tree before recording a negative. The commit, not the bank, is the trustworthy base -- which is the arbitration corollary of the run-34 lane-lock law that the commit is the first evidence an edit exists.
